title: Expose the exponential rebinding trap hidden by single-arm wash kinetics
statement: For m independent arms with n->n-1 at n*u, n->n+1 at (m-n)*a and0 an absorbing wash sink, u>0,a>=0, starting at m: E[T_m]=sum_{n=1}^m (1/(n*u))*sum_{j=n}^m C(m,j)/C(m,n)*(a/u)^(j-n). At a=0 this is H_m/u; for fixed a>0 its first summand gives E[T_m]>=((1+a/u)^m-1)/(m*a).

requires: Independent identical arms, fixed u>0 and a>=0, initial fully bound state, and a genuine absorbing wash sink at zero arms.
provides: For m independent arms with n->n-1 at n*u, n->n+1 at (m-n)*a and0 an absorbing wash sink, u>0,a>=0, starting at m: E[T_m]=sum_{n=1}^m (1/(n*u))*sum_{j=n}^m C(m,j)/C(m,n)*(a/u)^(j-n). At a=0 this is H_m/u; for fixed a>0 its first summand gives E[T_m]>=((1+a/u)^m-1)/(m*a).
assumptions: Cooperativity, arm geometry, nonsink reattachment and active displacement change the process. Source rates and finite-state numerical checks are hypothetical/reported.
costs: Clearance is a paid time and may grow exponentially with arm count. Actual displacement, sink, retained root and re-registration have their own chemistry/damage costs.
contract.units: u,a are inverse time; m,n,j are counts; E[T_m] is time.
contract.obstruction: Demonstrate multivalent island removal without destroying the product or its reusable positional guide.

body: Let Delta_n=T_n-T_(n-1). The backward equation gives n*u*Delta_n=1+(m-n)*a*Delta_(n+1), with Delta_m=1/(m*u). Iterate downwards and sum Delta_n to obtain the formula. The n=1 binomial sum yields the lower bound, proving exponential trapping for fixed positive a/u as m grows. Suppressing rebinding changes the kinetic law to the harmonic case, but active displacement and a selective sink must be acquired for the actual multi-adapter covalent island; a single-donor off-rate does not establish it.

evidence.range_scope: Independent-arm absorbing-sink birth-death clearance and exponential rebinding lower bound.
